findings.title: queued default is evaluated once at import, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated a single time when the module is imported, not when each instance is created. Dataclasses only reject clearly mutable defaults (list/dict/set), so a datetime default is accepted, but every AssignmentSource constructed without an explicit `queued` — including every call to `from_integration()` — will share the exact same timestamp equal to the process/module import time. The field therefore never records when an assignment was actually queued, so any future staleness, debounce, or ordering logic reading it will be wrong. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The accompanying `test_to_dict` only asserts `queued is not None`, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Raw datetime is put into Celery task kwargs via to_dict()
findings.body: `assignment_source.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which contains a raw `datetime` for `queued`, and that dict is placed directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`. Raw datetimes in Celery kwargs are only safe if the task serializer is pickle or a datetime-aware encoder; with a JSON serializer (Celery's default) publishing the task raises a serialization error inside `sync_group_assignee_outbound`, which is called from `GroupAssignee.assign`/`deassign` and would surface as a failure of the assignment itself. Even if a serializer round-trips it, `AssignmentSource.from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` without converting `queued` back to a datetime, so after a JSON round-trip the frozen dataclass holds a `str` where `datetime` is annotated, violating its type contract. The new tests run under `self.tasks()` (eager), which never serializes, so they cannot detect this.

findings.title: Loop-prevention tests only cover assign with a matching source
findings.body: The new test only covers `assign()` when the source integration matches. There is no test for `deassign()` with a matching source (even though `deassign` was given an `assignment_source` parameter and forwards it to `sync_group_assignee_outbound`), and no test verifying the stated behavior that a different integration still receives the outbound sync. The inbound tests (`test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign`/`_deassign`) call `sync_group_assignee_inbound` without `self.tasks()`, so they never execute or assert on the enqueued outbound tasks end-to-end. A regression in the source comparison for the deassign path or for non-matching integrations would pass the suite.

findings.title: from_dict fails open, silently disabling loop prevention
findings.body: `from_dict` catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None`. In `sync_assignee_outbound`, a `None` source simply means `should_sync` runs without the source comparison, i.e. the cycle-prevention guard is silently disabled and the outbound sync proceeds — the exact loop this PR is meant to stop. If a payload is ever malformed (e.g. an unexpected/renamed key during a partial deploy), the protection degrades silently rather than being logged or surfaced.

findings.title: sync_status_outbound gains an assignment_source parameter that is never supplied
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares an `assignment_source: AssignmentSource | None = None` argument, but no caller passes it and no status-sync path constructs an `AssignmentSource`, so the parameter is dead. It advertises a source-context contract to implementers that is never provided, and it does not actually prevent the analogous status-change sync cycle.

findings.title: New task kwarg breaks task signature during a rolling deploy
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` now accepts `assignment_source_dict`. During a rolling deploy, tasks published by already-updated web/API code (which include this kwarg) can be consumed by not-yet-updated workers whose function signature does not accept it, raising `TypeError`; the `@retry` wrapper will exhaust retries and drop the task, so outbound assignee propagation to other integrations is silently lost for the duration of the deploy.
